Legacy of Gods #2

God of Pain

Rina Kent

3.85
209,721 ratings20,142 reviews
Rate this book
Creighton King is silent, brooding, and hostile. Annika Volkov still has a crush on him. She is everything he is not: bright, lively, and the heart of every party. What Annika doesn’t realize is that behind Creighton’s quiet beauty lies a dark and violent soul.

Creighton knows he can never outrun his past, so he unleashes his pain on others. He never expected to be drawn to the girl who is his complete opposite. But as Annika tries to break through his walls, he finds himself captivated by her especially after he uncovers her wilder side. Now that he’s obsessed, she will never escape him.

Can Annika bring light to Creighton’s darkness, or will he pull her into the shadows with him?
    GenresDark RomanceRomanceDarkCollegeGrumpy SunshineAudiobookEnemies To Lovers

About the author

Rina Kent

65 books75.5k followers
Rina Kent is a New York Times, USA Today, and #1 bestselling author of all things dark romance.
Better known for writing unapologetic anti-heroes and villains, Rina weaves tales of characters you shouldn’t fall for but inevitably do. Her stories are laced with a touch of darkness, a splash of angst, and just the right amount of unhealthy intensity.
When she’s not busy plotting mayhem for her ever-expanding Rinaverse, she leads a private life in London, travels, and pampers her cats in true Cat Lady fashion.

So awesome!



The following ratings are out of 5:
Romance: 💚🖤💙💜❤️
Heat/Steam: 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥
Story/Plot: 📕📗📙📘📔
World building: 🌏🌍🌎🌍🌏
Character development: 😤😥😊🤩😘

The heroine: Annika Volkov - she is the daughter of Adrian Volkov and Lia Morelli and was born into the Bratva mafia. Her brother Jeremy will one day take over for their father and Annika knows that women in the mafia are used to make alliances through arranged marriages so she knows that will most likely be her fate one day. Meanwhile she is attending Royal Elite University as an art student. Her brother goes to the nearby Kings U and is very protective of her.

The Hero: Creighton King - He is the adopted son of British powerhouses Aiden King and Elsa Steel. He loves his family but feels that something is missing in him. It happened when he was three years old and saw his real parents massacred in front of him. He has deviant tastes and dark desires. He rarely speaks and is determined to find out what happened to his biological family.

The Story: Annika is like a tiny ray of sunshine around campus. She is talkative, bright and nice to everyone. Though she hides behind her bright sunny nature, she has OCD and yearns to live life on her own terms. She hangs around with a group of the elites of Royal Elite, The sons and daughters of Levi and Aiden King, Xander Knight, Ronan Astor, and Cole Nash. She loses interest in most people once she gets to know them, but Creighton King is a different story, he fascinates and scares her.



I won’t go any further into the story, but to say that Rina Kent is a master at getting you interested in dark and mysterious characters from the first words of her books. I get drawn into her stories from the first words and can’t wait to find out what these people will do. Creighton was a great anti-hero and is my new favorite book boyfriend! Annika was lovable and it was easy to empathize with her throughout the story.

There is a ton of chemistry between Creighton and Annika and though they are opposites, they are both interesting in their own way. Him for being the bad boy he is with a dark and mysterious past and her for being multi-faceted and hiding things behind such a cheerful disposition. I wanted to know everything about what these two had beneath the surface from the very start.



The world building is terrific and I just love this world. I thought I liked the world of Royal Elite School when Aiden King was there, but this world of Royal Elite University and Kings U is even better. This second generation are exactly everything I love about dark romance. So many of them are psychopaths and sociopaths and every one of the guys is a god in his own right. I can’t wait to read about every single one of them.

I voluntarily read & reviewed an advanced copy of this book. All thoughts & opinions are my own.

There’s a weight to God of Pain that lingers long after closing the book. It’s not about fleeting romance—it’s about choices, consequences, and the shadows that shape us. Every glance, every word between Anika and Creighton is charged with unspoken tension, a push and pull that makes their story feel alive ✨🥹

Somewhere in the middle, the truth hits: Lia, Anika’s mother, killed Creighton’s biological father to protect herself. That revelation stretches over their interactions, coloring each moment with danger, guilt, and the heavy weight of the past.

I found myself fully immersed in their struggles, feeling their frustrations, their moments of reckless courage, and the small, fragile flashes of vulnerability that made them unexpectedly human. This book didn’t just tell a story—it pressed itself into my thoughts, leaving me tangled in its darkness and compelled to revisit its world again and again. The tension, the longing, and the raw emotional stakes made it impossible to forget 🔥

you know what would’ve made this book better? if they both died at the end. washed out to sea, never to be heard from again. honestly that would’ve been a stronger plot than whatever this was supposed to be.

i genuinely don’t have the words to explain how stupid and unserious and dramatic this book is. it reads like a parody—and not in a good way. just pure cringe. i knew two paragraphs in that i was gonna hate it, and i was right. every chapter somehow managed to be more unhinged and more boring. it felt like a dare to stack every cliché imaginable into one book—and then double down on them.

annika was giving “my toxic trait is empathy” energy while unironically worshipping tchaikovsky (whoever that is). creighton was a blank slate with a superiority complex. and their relationship? awful from the start. we’ve got masked break ins, forced mouth grabbing, and instant obsession. like yeah, totally normal to get cornered in your room by a guy in a mask and somehow still end up emotionally attached. i wish i was exaggerating.

and the plot?? genuinely what plot. it was just a string of dramatic nonsense like surprise fires, forced cohabitation, multiple kidnappings, weird family drama, and let’s not forget the part where she literally shoots him—and somehow that ends up pulling them closer. like “lol sorry for shooting you, let’s go trauma bond on a private island where i’m not allowed to call for help because you kidnapped me.” what are we doing.

the writing didn’t help either. i’m sorry but i physically recoiled when i read “you’ve been wiggling this little arse for weeks and it’s time to discipline it.” writing that out just now made me want to run into traffic. there’s just no way to take any of this seriously. it wasn’t even fun bad. it’s just so dramatic it flattened any actual tension, and when something serious did happen, i couldn’t even care.

there were maybe two things that mildly held my attention, and that’s being generous. the rest? completely forgettable. at this point i’m only here for book 5 because i’ve already made it this far and need to see it through. but after hating both this and the first one, i’m thinking maybe i’m just not a rina kent girl. the writing doesn’t work for me, the characters don’t work for me, and mafia romance? yeah, that might be on me.

maybe it’s the whiplash of going from angsty sports romances to whatever this was, but i am so unwell. this book drained me. and yet i will still be reading the next one because unfortunately i have no self control and need to know how deep this rabbit hole goes. pray for me.

This book – I devoured it in one sitting and just under 6 hours. I left sleep alone and focused solely on this incredible book. I couldn’t put it down, I needed answers and resolutions.

I really liked God of Malice but I fucking loved God of Pain. This is by far so much better than God of Malice and it’s all because of Annika and Creighton.

You know Creighton was clueless on how he felt about her when he showed up in her room after that attempted arson and touched her face. How he thought she wasn’t in his thoughts before is beyond me?

Annika has become one of my favorite FMC's, her mom Lia is still at the top though and the Deception Trilogy still reigns supreme and seeing Adrian made me scream way too loud. He was still madly in love with Lia, madly obsessive and possessive and of course madly protective. I loved that we got both his and Lia’s POV chapters.

Watching Creigh go from living inside a shell to embracing so much around him that even people who have known him all his life were utterly shocked by his actions. He staked his claim towards Anni in front of everyone and just couldn’t stand anybody taking up her thoughts or time that wasn’t him.

The way that it mainly starts for them is when Annika decides she needs a fake boyfriend to show that she is ''in love'' and won't be forced into an arranged marriage. She knows her dad would never allow it if she loves someone. She asks Bran or Remi at first and not Creighton which causes him to go balistic. He wonders why it can't be him and so the cat/mouse game begins.

They go on dates and spend more time together. He pretends to like her gross cooking and entertains her date ideas. He talks to her and opens up. That bathtub scene was heartbreaking.

The subtle moments they shared before they become a couple - my favorite has to be the part where they have a picnic and dance on the rain. Their first kiss. Hers and HIS. Yes, our Creigh has devious tendencies towards women but it’s all control and inflicting pain. Kissing wasn’t something he wanted to do but with Anni it was all he wanted.

''I kiss her like I've never kissed before, because I have never kissed before, never considered the act of any value-not until this wrecking ball bulldozed through my life''

The ways they fell so comfortably into a relationship. He didn’t fight it after realizing she was good for him. He didn’t feel like she was trying to change him. They did have tough moments when he opened up his past, but they got through it. His custom-made purple diamond necklace for his birthday! The kitten she was taking care of being her next gift as he it for her! Argh bless him.

The scene where he claims her in front of everyone was amazing. He tells them they have gone on dates and can't help but touch her for everyone to see then kisses her so they know she is his.

''She's mine. if I find out either of you touched her, prepare to lose a limb''

The spice – listen this was top notch. It was amazing and made me blush way too many times.

''You're the only one I want. Everyone else is just white noise.''
''He treats me like a princess in public and his custom-made whore in private.''

I knew that his past had to be related to the Mafia, but I was sure that he was probably part of the Irish Mafia or something and never did I imagine his father was Richard – the candidate that was in the pocket of the Mafia and who also took advantage of helpless and one day decided to attach and try to sexually assault Lia which caused his death certificate. His wife (Creigh’s mother) was even more in deep shit. She was in cahoots with her husband in such a disturbing way that when he died, she was left to deal with the aftermath and decided to kill herself by hanging and kill 3-year-old Creigh by gas. He got away. He remembers ALL of the events of that night – seeing his mother hanging, all of it haunts him and he wants revenge.

When he finds out about Annika’s parents being connected to his childhood trauma, he wants to take matters into his own hands and avenge not his parents who considers to be trash but avenge the 3-year-old little helpless boy who was shaped by what happened.

I do not think ANYBODY will see that twist coming, I also do not think anybody will see the events that transpired after he confronted Jeremy. He basically goes off and just wants it all to end, knowing he can’t have Anni after the truth is revealed is devastating, he wants to die, and he provoked an Anni who has a gun (we find out before that she has excellent aim and never misses) she comes flying down to the basement where Landon has kidnapped Nikolai and lured in Jeremy.
She is forced and provoked to shoot Creigh – yes, you read that right. She SHOOTS him right in the chest to save her brother who he stabbed in the arm. Creigh did it to make it all end and die.

As she never misses, she doesn’t hit his heart and he recover but she is ousted by his family and friends and Adrian my darling comes to the UK to take her away. Where he has a showdown with Aiden. I know Aiden is a psycho, but Adrian is worse in my eyes. In a fight who would win? For me it’s Adrian no doubt.

Creighton telling Eli what she means to him before coming up with his plan:
''I like spending time with her. She's the light I never thought I needed and the one person who can fill up the hollowness.''

Anni goes back to NYC and it’s a month until she sees him again where he enlists the help of Cecily to lure her away and kidnap her (Cecily did not know about the kidnapping plan). Takes her to the island owned by his grandfather and they spend weeks together. He wants her to pick him and choose him in the moments he believes she would always choose her family. Their relationship is severely strained and suffers because of the darkness looming over them.

Adrian AGAIN shows up (never stop showing up) and is determined to hurt/kill Creigh for kidnapping his daughter and harming her. Anni finally realizing at that moment that all Creigh wanted was to know he would once be chosen over what she knows, and loves decides to take matters into her own hands and point the gun to herself and threaten death. Creigh admits he loves her, and she ever dies he would follow right after (dramatic in reality but in books it’s what we want to hear lol).

''I would rather die than live without you''

''You win, little purple''
''I win?''
''All of me. My heart, body, and soul are yours.''

''I love you, Annika. I love you to the point I see darkness without you and light only when I'm with you. You're my sanctuary and the one person who makes me whole''

She finally relents and Adrian finally agrees to take them both away and not cause harm. I loved seeing Creigh rile up Adrian the way Yan does. Threatening him that he will marry Anni and give him grandkids- a threat in the epilogue he tells Anni he will need to tell her that it will become a reality. So I guess they will be the first ones to get hitched maybe??

- We get great cameos from Yan and Kolya (loyal guards of Adrian and Lia’s).
- We do get Adrian and Lia (that's all I really asked for tbh)
- We don’t get to see Glyn and Killian a lot (which made me happy they didn’t take away from the story).
- We do not get anything from Mia which means nothing from her and Landon. Landon does cause a lot of problems though.
- We do get more moments from Brandon and Nikolai – especially in the basement.
- We do get Eli and Ava moments – Ava mostly hating him lol and Eli being a incredibly big brother.
- We do get scenes with Aiden and Elsa (including Jonathan, Agnus, and Ethan).
- We do get Jeremy and Cecily crumbs <<<< This has to be the next couple. The epilogue has Cecily try to tell Anni something in secret but gets interrupted by Creigh. She was spooked. I should mention that when she helped Creighton get Annika, she had to face the wrath of Jeremy, and something had to have happened – also it is again stated that she sneaks out in the middle of the night. Where is she going??

Overall as you can tell I loved this. I wish I hadn't finished it so quickly but it's been such an incredible journey.

Can't wait to see which couple is next in God of Wrath!

This review contains some spoilers, but I think this book isn't that worthy of your time, so feel free to see my honest opinion.

What a nightmare. When I saw the arc team saying that this book has so much pain I was waiting for something sad and heartbreaking, not pathetic and boring.

I had high expectations for God of Pain, and I'm not trying to be a bitch, but Rina pretty please stop writing. You don't need to write 3 books per year, because you're doing a shit job. I can not believe this woman wrote AdrianLia.

I gonna write an essay, because I have various points that I hated.

Let's start with Creighton and Annika's relationship, I liked so much the start of the book, but so in the half, Rina just stopped and the book keep being the same, with so many unnecessary scenes with their boring and stressful friends (read Remi the king of being annoying, Cecily the girl who doesn't have a personality, Landon who keep trying so hard to be a bad boy, etc). Yeah, we get some cute moments between Creighton and Annika, but I didn't understand how they love each other.

Now the kink, what are the dark and violent tendencies of Creigh? In the scene with Landon we see some more dark shit, but with Annika the only thing he does is slap her ass. Oh Creigh, so dark and violent, gonna slap Annika's ass (scary AF). Really, Rina? You do all the promotion of the book about Creigh being dark and we get just some ropes??? Not even a candle or knife. NOTHING. This isn't a kink book in any way.

I'm having nightmares about all the bad boys' images that Rina wants to pass. Like, what do they do that they're so bad? My five-month-old dog is worse than them. Like, Creigh wants revenge and he just stabs Jeremy's arm. AND THE WORST, "the" Jeremy Volkov just goes for a trap and enters without a gun. The part Nikolai tries to kill himself had more violence than the Elite pathetic attempt at kidnapping.
I'm annoyed with all the talk of they're psychopaths, crazy boys, the devil, so scary, and keep going the list of references Rina made of her boys (by her girls who did grow with them but are like little cats scared) and they're just kids playing of being mafiosos. I don't believe Annika is the only person in this kidnap scene with a gun. THE ONLY, THE PURPLE GIRL IS THE ONLY PERSON WITH A GUN (IN A ROOM WITH PSYCHOPATHS).

I gonna even talk about the fiasco that Rina made of that shot, It was not that deep. I laugh all the scene, because really? She was protecting her brother (the guy who always was in her life) from the guy who "loved" her and almost killed her brother because of his petty revenge. And I say petty because he had a family who loved him (and he has been dumb enough to risk his family's life, because Adrian definitely wasn't letting this go) for the fact he had some hard time? And let's remember that the family who loved him had him because of Adrian.

But if you ask what made me drop my note to 2 stars, I gonna say, the kidnapping. Fuck, Creighton just decided to kidnap Annika of her family because of his petty jealousy (how can Annika save her brother and not choose his revenge on behalf of a rapist), and they just keep fucking for one week before Rina changes the song and Annika try to kill herself (nonsense again, we don't have a construction, is just one day she's all smiles and talking and good and the next she's like "I gonna kill myself because I cannot live with who you're now...".
But the most laughable part of the kidnapping? Creighton thinks Adrian doesn't gonna find them. Bro, you're on your grandpa's island, not on another planet.

I'm really sad and annoyed with all the universe, the second generation is honestly a bunch of spoiled rich kids who Rina is trying to force mental illness (like Annika saying she has OCD, I have OCD and this isn't OCD bitch) to justify the bad behavior ( and they look like toddlers doing pranks).

So why I gave it two stars? The family's scenes (like Eli and Creigh). I hope Rina stops trying so hard to make the image of her characters and learns to pass them by actions.
